officers.name: Jawad Zaza
officers.bio: Jawad Zaza is an Electrical & Computer Engineering student preparing to transfer in Spring 2027. He joined AEC in his first semester and worked his way up from Social Media Director to Workshop Director before becoming President, where he built the club's first funded team for the CSU California Unmanned Aerial Systems Competition (C-UASC) and led development of its autonomous UAV. His engineering experience extends beyond AEC through internships at Paradyne Medical and UC Irvine's Industrial Assessment Center. As President, Jawad is passionate about turning AEC into a launchpad for hands-on engineering experience and helping members find their own path into the field.

officers.name: Samuel Giron
officers.bio: Samuel is a mechanical engineering student who joined AEC a year ago and quickly became Flight Systems Hardware Lead for the CUASC drone team. He plans to transfer to Cal Poly Pomona next year. As Co-President, Samuel is passionate about making engineering approachable, sharing the excitement of hands-on problem-solving, and helping identify motivated members who can contribute to future competition teams.

officers.name: Jane Nguyen
officers.bio: Jane Nguyen is an Electrical Engineering student preparing to transfer in Spring 2027. Through AEC’s C-UASC autonomous UAV project, she has transformed classroom concepts into hands-on engineering experience while learning through experimentation and collaboration. As an officer, Jane is committed to expanding practical projects, strengthening industry connections, and creating opportunities for students at every experience level to build confidence, explore engineering, and discover what they can accomplish.

officers.name: Mary Michael
officers.bio: Mary Michael is a third-year Aerospace Engineering student at Fullerton College who joined AEC in Fall 2025 and plans to transfer after Spring 2027. She values the club as a place to connect with peers who share her academic and professional interests. Mary’s vision is to foster a close-knit community where students strengthen their teamwork skills, collaborate as engineers, and build meaningful friendships that extend beyond the classroom.
